# BLO-43344 — report declared MCP servers that never connect

[BLO-43344](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-43344) /
[#2487](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2487)

A server declared in `adapterConfig.mcpServers` that fails to connect contributes
no `mcp__<name>__*` tools and says nothing. Its absence is then indistinguishable
from a tool the agent was never meant to have, so it reads as deliberate policy.
The CTO's `k8s-rw` binding went missing that way across three runs and roughly two
months, and each run concluded the capability was ungranted. It was granted and
bound the whole time.

The `claude` CLI does report it: the `system`/`init` event carries every declared
server with the connection status it reached. `parseClaudeStreamJson` read
`session_id` and `model` off that event and discarded `mcp_servers`, which is the
only surface distinguishing "declared but dead" from "never declared".

Changed:

- `src/server/parse.ts` — keep `mcp_servers` from the init event and return it as
  `mcpServers` on both the early-return and normal paths. A resumed session's
  later init replaces the list rather than appending to it. Absent when the CLI
  emits no `mcp_servers`, so an older CLI stays silent instead of reporting every
  server as failed.
- `src/server/execute.ts` — after parsing the stream, log any server whose status
  is not `connected`, by name and status, alongside the ones that did connect.
  Logged, not raised: a dead MCP server degrades a run but does not fail it, and
  failing here would turn one unreachable endpoint into a fleet-wide outage —
  which is why the log call itself goes through `logQuietly`, so a rejecting sink
  cannot become the throw site this block exists to avoid. Emitted above the
  `jobTimedOut` return so a run that spun on a missing tool namespace still
  reports it. Server names are `JSON.stringify`d into the `[paperclip] ` line so
  a name carrying a newline cannot forge a second one.
- `src/server/parse.test.ts` — coverage for the statuses surviving the parse, for
  the resumed-session replace, for a later init with no `mcp_servers` leaving the
  earlier list intact, and for an init with no `mcp_servers` at all.

Vendor-local change, no upstream counterpart.
